designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, consistent-stroke vector icons on a tight 4x5 grid with a bold condensed headline; separates and prints trivially in one ink and reads instantly from 3 m. The joke lands, but the piece is a tidy icon sheet more than a drawing, and the small condensed labels (and the thin serif ABS) are the weak point once white ink on black gains and fills.
designs.fix: Enlarge and slightly embolden the label type (about 20%) and redraw the ABS letters in the same stroke weight as the icons so every name holds up in white ink on the black tee.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Charming, confident brush drawings with real variety in pose; the repeated 'Turn around.' and the quiet '7. Sigh.' deliver a warm, specific joke, and the single-ink line art is ideal for screen print. On the tee it prints small and airy, and the light serif title and tapered brush tips sit near the edge of what holds at that scale.
designs.fix: Scale the whole print up about 15-20% on the chest/back and bump the title to a heavier weight so the tapered strokes and caption type keep their bite.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Strong, even-weight line art with an expressive tabby and clear three-panel storytelling; the bed breaking out of panel 3 is a nice touch and it separates cleanly. But the cat-prefers-the-box gag is a well-worn one, the big numerals hanging left make the column lopsided, and the dense tabby stripes plus hairline bed creases may fill or drop out at print size.
designs.fix: Give it a fresher twist or caption beat (or tuck the numerals into the panel corners to centre the column), and thicken the bed's crease hairlines to a printable minimum.
